glossary.m: the big lesson a story teaches, said as a full sentence
what a story is about, in a word or two, like loyalty or winter
the words characters say out loud in a story
the marks “ and ” that go around the exact words someone says
the part that tells who is talking, like said Lucy
the main part of a word that holds its meaning, like ject, which means throw
a part added to the front or the end of a word, like un- or -ed
telling the truth, even when it is hard

cards.title: World Notes: A Lion’s Roar
cards.sub: A real thing behind the story
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read the chapter with your lens in mind.
text: A real lion’s roar is one of the loudest sounds any animal makes. On a quiet night it can be heard about five miles away.
Lions roar to tell other lions, This is our land. They also roar to call their family group, called a pride, back together.
In Chapter 13, Aslan gives a great roar, and the Witch runs for her life.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it's Opti. In Chapter 13, Edmund is rescued, and the Witch comes to talk with Aslan. Watch for big ideas forming.
transcripts.guide1: Word work first: the root ject, the marks around spoken words, and long words built from parts.
transcripts.guide2: Read Chapter 13 with your lens. Then answer three questions.

notes.wordParts: The root ject means throw. reject = throw back. inject = throw into. eject = throw out. project = throw forward.
notes.grammar: Quotation marks go around the exact words someone says. The first word gets a capital. The comma or period goes inside the closing mark: “Let him approach,” said Aslan.
notes.spelling: A long word is often a root with parts added. Find the root first: un + expect + ed = unexpected.
notes.wgrd: A topic is one word, like loyalty. A theme is a full sentence about it: The story shows that forgiveness can give someone a fresh start.
vocab: someone who betrays the trust of their own side
to make up for a wrong you have done
giving up something precious for something or someone more important

plate.alt: A painting of a snowy hilltop with three old, bare oak trees around a low table of big stones
plate.credit: Dolmen in the Snow · Caspar David Friedrich, 1807 · Galerie Neue Meister, Dresden · Public domain
plate.look: A painting by Caspar David Friedrich, a German painter, from 1807. Under the old oak trees is a dolmen: a big flat stone resting on standing stones, built by people more than 5,000 years ago. In Chapter 13, the Witch comes to meet Aslan on the hill beside the Stone Table.

mods.script: Let's fix a sentence. The correct one first. Let him approach, said Aslan. The words Aslan says sit inside the quotation marks. Let starts with a capital, and the comma goes inside, before the closing mark. Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or Sentence B, and type it the right way.

mods.todo: Think about the question. Tap See if you were right. Type the missing part in each box.
mods.script: [curious] A throw is hiding inside this word. Projectile. Pro means forward. Ject means throw. A projectile is something thrown forward, like a snowball. Read the four words and their parts, and tap See if you were right. Then type the missing part in each box.

mods.script: Be a word detective with me. Earnestly. Here's the sentence. The Lion and the Witch talked earnestly together in low voices. One, read the sentence: everyone is waiting, and worried. Two, look for word parts: earnest, l y. Three, check it. Earnestly means in a very serious way. Read how we figured out the first word. Then fill in each sentence with a word from the word bank, and tap Check My Work. Last, play the matching game.

items.t: Edmund says “I’m sorry” to each of his brother and sisters.
items.why: He tells the truth about what he did wrong.

items.t: Aslan says the Witch is right about the Deep Magic, even though it is bad news.
items.why: He does not pretend, even when the truth is hard.
